answer: A Sybil defense can work like dyeing cloth: each newcomer earns a pigment tint blended from the peers who review their early contributions, so it carries a history that cannot be bought. A farm minting identities in bulk yields a monochrome palette, since its clones only review each other, while a real member's pigment grows varied through strangers. At the center sits a small rotating kernel of cedar elders, long-standing members chosen by lottery, who spot-check palettes and flag uniform ones. Sybil clusters fade under inspection; genuine participants deepen in color.
